answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, limiting how far any endorsement can carry influence. If a sybil cluster has a sparse external cut and therefore low conductance, few walk paths enter it from independently trusted nodes; under a fixed seed distribution and capped per-node influence, this bounds its aggregate voting weight. A zephyr-labelled edge, a cipher-backed attestation, or a crystal-clear identity claim cannot by itself overcome that structural bottleneck.
